title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X is a variety (on the next page, an anabelian curve) over a field K of finite type over Q, with Γ = Gal(K̄/K). Let C = Π̂_1(X,I) be the profinite étale fundamental groupoid of X_K̄, based at a set I of points with I ⊂ X_K. Γ acts on C. Grothendieck asks for intrinsic conditions on an automorphism Θ of C, acting trivially on objects, for Θ to come from some u ∈ Γ.

Opening paragraph. This finishes the computation on the previous page. There, liftings of Θ to a covering groupoid C' were parametrised by the quotient Transp_{Π0}(Π'0, Θ(Π'0))/Π'0. When C' = Π̂_1(X'_K̄, I') with I' = p^{-1}(I) for a finite étale cover p: X' → X, there is no freedom in choosing I'. The lifting condition is 'algebraic of the simplest kind'. If one also requires the lift Θ' to be the identity on the objects I', the lift is unique, and the only extra condition is that Θ~ acts trivially on I'.

Necessary conditions for Θ to come from some u ∈ Γ.
(a) For every finite étale cover X' → X defined over K, with I' = X'|I (the inverse image), there is a lift Θ~ of Θ to Π̂_1(X',I') that is the identity on the K-rational objects I' ∩ X'_K. This holds for Galois actions, because u fixes K-rational points.
(b) For every hyperbolic curve Y over K, every K-morphism f: X' → Y and every x' ∈ I' ∩ X'_K, the image of π̂_1(X',x') → π̂_1(Y,f(x')) must be stable under Θ~ (for a suitable Θ~). More generally, for x' not K-rational, choose ν ≥ 1 with Θ^ν x' = x'. The image must then be stable under Θ^ν, which mimics the open subgroup of Γ fixing x'.

Grothendieck calls these conditions 'draconian'. The margin NB notes that the conditions depend only on Θ as an operation on π̂_1(X,t0), t0 ∈ I. On the next page he says it is 'not too unreasonable' to conjecture they are sufficient for an anabelian curve over a finitely generated K. He adds that u should be unique when K is algebraic over Q. In positive transcendence degree one must at least assume K is finite over the field of moduli of X, and he does not know whether uniqueness then holds.

What this amounts to: a single-variety, arithmetic analogue of characterising the image of Galois in the automorphisms of the fundamental-group tower. The ingredients are compatibility with all finite étale covers (with rational base points fixed) and compatibility with all maps to hyperbolic curves. This is an early form of the Ihara / Oda–Matsumoto ('I/OM') type question.
errors: Condition (b) as written is imprecise. Θ~ acts on the groupoid of X', not a priori on π̂_1(Y). So 'the image is stable under Θ~*' needs either an induced action on Y's groupoid (his '(pour Θ~ convenable!)') or the reformulation that the kernel of π̂_1(X',x') → π̂_1(Y,f(x')) is Θ~-stable, so that Θ~ descends to the image. The kernel version is the intrinsic one.

The phrase 'on dispose pas du choix de I'' is elliptic. The meaning is that I' is forced to be p^{-1}(I), so the transporter freedom of the previous page reduces to the requirement Θ~|I' = id. This is consistent, not an error.

ideas.what: Lifting a groupoid automorphism to the covering groupoid of a finite étale cover with base set the full fibre p^{-1}(I); the lift is unique if required to be the identity on objects, subject to the condition that it acts trivially on I'.
ideas.modern_name: Lifting automorphisms along coverings of profinite groupoids (transporter / Galois-category formalism)
ideas.where_published: Galois-category formalism in SGA1 V; groupoids with many base points in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Necessary conditions for an automorphism of Π̂_1(X,I) to be Galois: liftability to all finite étale covers over K, fixing K-rational base points, plus stability of images/kernels of π_1 under all maps to hyperbolic curves (with Θ^ν for non-rational points).
ideas.modern_name: 'Geometric' or 'morphism-compatible' automorphisms of étale fundamental groups; I/OM (Ihara / Oda–Matsumoto) type characterisation of G_K
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara; Oda–Matsumoto (I/OM question, ~1990); Pop (proofs of birational/tripod versions, 2010s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only discusses characterising Γ via the Teichmüller tower / GT, not these single-variety conditions

ideas.what: Conjecture (stated on next page) that these conditions suffice for an anabelian curve over a finitely generated field. Uniqueness of u is expected over number fields; in positive transcendence degree it needs K finite over the field of moduli, and is left open there.
ideas.modern_name: Galois characterisation conjecture for a single anabelian curve; injectivity of G_K → Out(π_1^geom)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Injectivity: Belyi / Matsumoto / Hoshi–Mochizuki; characterisation: I/OM (Ihara, Oda–Matsumoto), Pop

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, for ONE variety/anabelian curve X over a finitely generated field K, explicit criteria for an automorphism of the profinite fundamental groupoid to come from Gal(K̄/K). The criteria are: lifts to all finite étale covers that fix K-rational base points, plus stability of π_1-images under all K-maps to hyperbolic curves (with Θ^ν for points rational over extensions). He then conjectures sufficiency. This is a single-curve, arithmetic-base-point variant of the I/OM question, predating Ihara/Oda–Matsumoto. The known theorems (Pop) concern the whole category of varieties over Q̄ or birational/tripod towers, not this single-variety criterion with rational-point conditions.
missed.quote: on trouve donc une condition nécessaire pour qu'une action Θ de C triviale sur les objets provienne d'un u ∈ Γ ... Ce sont là des conditions draconiennes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a 'local' (one curve plus its covers and maps to hyperbolic curves) version of the I/OM problem. It uses K-rational points as rigid objects, linking it to the section conjecture. Whether such a criterion holds for a single hyperbolic curve over a number field appears to be open and not explicitly formulated in the literature.

missed.claim: The condition that Θ~ be the identity on K-rational objects of every cover is a groupoid way of saying that rational points give Galois-fixed objects. This directly links the characterisation of the Galois image to the section conjecture / rational-point combinatorics inside the same framework.
missed.quote: et qui est l'identité sur I' ∩ X'_K
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Combining section-conjecture data (rational points as fixed base points) with I/OM-type compatibility is not a standard formulation; it may give a usable criterion in anabelian geometry.

deep.surprise_reason: An explicit, early (from 1978 on) formulation of necessary — and conjecturally sufficient — conditions characterising Galois automorphisms of the fundamental groupoid of a single anabelian variety. It anticipates the I/OM question in a single-variety, rational-point-sensitive form not found in his published texts. It is sketchy and imprecise, though, and close in spirit to later work by Ihara, Oda–Matsumoto and Pop.
transcription_corrections: 'que pour I' = p^{-1}(I) on dispose [?] pas du choix de I' i.e. de I' — the sense is that one has no choice of I' (it is forced by I).
'pour H hyperb.' is most likely 'pour Y hyperb.' (the target curve Y of f: X' → Y).
Top marginal letters before the struck-out 'il y a une action' read 'u ∈ Γ :' (continuing the sentence 'provienne d'un u ∈ Γ :').
'Θ~*' in condition (b) may be 'Θ~^*' (the induced action on fundamental groups).

Last line plausibly: 'Je pense que ce n'est pas trop déraisonnable,' continuing with 'conjecturer que ces conditions sont suffisantes' on the next page (the next-page transcription has 'nécessaires', which is likely an error for 'suffisantes').
